thread:
maria: FYI - ACME (tenant T-ACME) opened a support case: sudden p99 latency spikes + 504s on homepage model calls since 04:12 UTC. They pasted OOM-style errors. Can runtime/sre triage?
ryan-cust: our app hit p99 ~5.2s, p95 ~1.1s starting 04:12. Errors in our logs: 
```
2026-02-18T04:12:37Z model[worker-07]: kv_alloc failed: cannot satisfy 12MB alloc, free=8MB
2026-02-18T04:12:38Z model[worker-07]: oom signal raised, slab_fragmentation=0.74, alloc_retries=3
2026-02-18T04:12:39Z gateway: downstream 504 for /v1/generate
```
We've been using gpt-j-4b-quant q8, pinned revision r2026. Long-ish contexts (avg tokens ~1200). Not sure if our prompt encoder changed recently.
maria: adding details — tenant_id T-ACME, model gpt-j-4b-quant:r2026, region us-west-2, burst traffic from a new A/B test.
ash: (typo correction) -> ashok: taking this. First pass: looks like KV growth + fragmentation. Can you share a sample request payload and the exact time window of elevated p99?
ryan-cust: sample request (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate
{ "model":"gpt-j-4b-quant:r2026", "input":"<~1200 token user history + system prompt>", "max_tokens":512 }
```
Window 04:12:00 - 04:22:00, ~3% of calls failed with 504, p99 jumped from 0.9s to 5.2s.
ashok: thanks. ops-bot alert also fired: "GPU OOM signals on gpu-07 at 04:12:36 (5 events)". ops-bot: GPU memory usage 98%, slab fragmentation 0.72, kv_entries per-tenant spiked for T-ACME from 40k -> 210k in 5m.
jordyn: preliminary mitigation we can trigger now: 1) enable tenant-specific active fallback to a smaller model variant (gpt-j-4b-int8) 2) temporarily throttle long-context requests for T-ACME 3) trigger slab compaction on affected hosts. Which one do you want us to run immediately?
samir: I recommend fallback + throttle first, compaction next (compaction is heavier). Command to set fallback: `rictl route update --tenant T-ACME --fallback gpt-j-4b-int8 --reason "support: p99 spike"`
ashok: also toggling KV eviction policy for tenant: `rictl kv evict --tenant T-ACME --threshold 0.75 --strategy lru` — this will aggressively evict old prefixes to reclaim KV memory.
maria: ACME approved the fallback & throttle. They want minimal app changes.
ryan-cust: please keep us updated, we prefer fallback over throttling if possible.
jordyn: applied fallback + throttle at 04:18 UTC. Observed immediate drop in alloc failures on gpu-07 in logs. Running compaction now (low-priority background): `rictl slab compact --host gpu-07 --background`
ops-bot: update: fallback active for tenant T-ACME (04:18:12), throttle long-context requests >800 tokens (04:18:25).
ashok: metric dive: KV size per-tenant graph shows repeated sustained growth because A/B tests started sending many independent long-context sessions without reusing prefixes -> KV growth + fragmentation. Root hypothesis: workload pattern changed -> allocator failed to reuse freed small chunks -> fragmentation rose -> larger contiguous allocs fail (OOM).
samir: suggested allocator tuning (follow-up, not immediate): 1) reduce per-tenant max_kv_capacity from 1.2GB -> 800MB 2) enable `slab_merge=true` to coalesce free slabs 3) reduce growth_factor from 2.0 -> 1.25 to avoid sudden large allocs 4) add per-call kv_hint to avoid prefix retention when not needed.
ashok: repro steps we've documented to validate locally (runtime team):
1) spawn a worker with gpt-j-4b-quant q8 on test host (gpu-09)
2) flood with sequence of long-context unique sessions (script attached) generating ~200k unique prefixes across 5 minutes
3) watch kv_entries metrics and slab_fragmentation -> expect fragmentation >0.6 and `kv_alloc failed` after ~3-5m
Example load command: `python tools/load_gen.py --tenant T-ACME --sessions 200000 --ctx 1200 --concurrency 200`
Example log grep: `grep -A2 "kv_alloc failed" /var/log/runtime/worker-09.log`
jordyn: we've run the local repro on staging and reproduced fragmentation -> verified that enabling slab_merge + lowering growth_factor avoids OOM at same load, but increases average allocation latency slightly. Tradeoff notes captured.
maria: ACME confirmed fallbacks removed errors, p99 returned to ~1.0s after 12m. They want route-level guardrails so this doesn't recur.
ashok: next actions (owners):
- ashok: create PR to add per-tenant auto-fallback rules and a knob to auto-throttle long-context bursts (ETA 2d)
- jordyn: schedule allocator tuning rollout to 10% hosts + monitor (ETA 3d)
- samir: add a runtime alert for per-tenant KV-entry growth rate (>10k/min sustained) (ETA 1d)
- maria: close support case after confirmation from customer, send remediation summary
ryan-cust: thanks team, appreciate the quick response. Can we get a short postmortem once root cause + permanent fix are in?
maria: yes, we'll follow up with a short incident summary and the PR links. Closing notes: immediate mitigation = fallback + throttle + compaction. Root cause = KV growth from A/B workload + high slab fragmentation; long-term = allocator/eviction tuning + routing guardrails. :white_check_mark:
